Data Storage & External Services

Catalog records are persisted in SQL Server through Entity Framework. Image assets use Azure Blob Storage when configured; the alternative image service serves local Pics assets. Redis is configured as a session-state provider. Azure Active Directory supplies OpenID Connect authentication, while configuration builders support environment variables, user secrets, and an optional Key Vault source. Application Insights receives telemetry.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or database-backed catalog services, image storage, and managed-identity or connection-string SQL access from application settings.
  • CatalogService owns catalog operations and uses a scoped CatalogDBContext; there is no separate repository layer.
  • The UI and data services are deployed as one Web Forms application; no API gateway or service-to-service topology is present.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is the catalog response and form model; it references CatalogBrand and CatalogType. PaginatedItemsViewModel packages a page of catalog results. The ASMX upload response is an anonymous JSON object with name and url properties. No dedicated request/response DTO layer, OpenAPI specification, protobuf schema, or GraphQL schema was found. JSON serialization for upload responses uses JavaScriptSerializer; Web Forms page models are mutable classes.

Communication Patterns

Page and service calls are synchronous in-process calls. CatalogService accesses SQL Server through EF6; image operations use Azure Blob Storage or local files. OpenID Connect redirects to Azure Active Directory and maintains an application cookie. There are no discovered message-broker calls, service discovery mechanisms, API gateway composition, circuit breakers, retry policies, or application-level load balancing. SQL can use a configured connection string or an Azure managed-identity access token. The pics blob container is configured for public blob reads to support image delivery. HTTPS/TLS is not configured in the inspected application source and is expected to be supplied by hosting.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports an online product catalog: visitors browse and inspect items, while authenticated users maintain catalog products and their images. Catalog brands and types classify each item.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog managementA product available for browsing and inventory trackingBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog managementBrand classification for productsCan be associated with many CatalogItems
CatalogTypeCatalog managementType/category classification for productsCan be associated with many CatalogItems

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedWebFormsCatalog managementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server for persistence; Azure Blob Storage or local files for images; Azure AD for sign-in

All business data is owned by the single web application. There are no separate domain services or cross-context event exchanges.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse catalog

  1. A visitor opens /Default or a paginated catalog route.
  2. The page reads the route’s page index and page size, or applies the default page values.
  3. CatalogService loads ordered items and associated brand/type data through CatalogDBContext, or uses the configured mock service.
  4. The image service resolves each item’s display URI; the page binds the results and renders pagination.

Workflow 2: Maintain a catalog item

  1. A user opens a create, edit, or delete page. The page initiates an OpenID Connect challenge if the request is unauthenticated.
  2. Create and edit postbacks bind form values to a CatalogItem and proceed only when ModelState.IsValid.
  3. CatalogItem annotations constrain price format/range and stock values; brand and type selections are associated with the item.
  4. Create assigns an identifier using the HiLo SQL sequence before saving; edit marks the entity modified; delete removes the selected item.
  5. Successful changes redirect to the catalog home page.

Workflow 3: Upload a product image

  1. The browser posts a file and optional item ID to PicUploader.UploadImage.
  2. The service loads the image using Image.FromStream and accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF formats.
  3. The selected image service uploads or resolves the image and returns a URI; create/edit workflows associate its temporary name with a product.
  4. Azure image storage copies a temporary blob to the item-specific blob name after the catalog operation.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No inter-service aggregation or service-to-service calls were found. Catalog pages obtain entities through the local catalog service and EF6 context. Image metadata is associated with a catalog item, while image bytes live in the selected image store. If Azure storage is disabled, the mock image service resolves local images instead.

Business Workflow Sequence

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Price must use a positive numeric representation with at most two decimal places and must fit the configured range.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock are constrained to the annotated range from zero through ten million.
  • New catalog item IDs are generated from a SQL HiLo sequence in database mode.
  • Catalog items require a brand and type relationship; the database mapping enforces both associations.
  • Only JPEG, PNG, and GIF image formats are accepted by the upload endpoint.
  • Create/update postbacks save only when Web Forms ModelState.IsValid; deletion removes the selected item.
  • EF6 SaveChanges provides the persistence boundary. No distributed transaction, saga, audit trail, or business-event workflow was identified.
  • Page handlers initiate OpenID Connect sign-in for unauthenticated users; role-specific authorization rules were not identified.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy Web Forms, OWIN, and packages.config package management. The dependency set includes older versions of Entity Framework, Azure libraries, Application Insights, and authentication components; migration to modern .NET requires a framework and application-model transition rather than a simple package update.

Notable Observations

  • The package manifest includes many System.* and Microsoft.Extensions compatibility packages, increasing upgrade coordination effort.
  • Redis session and Azure storage are optional runtime integrations; their packages are declared even when mock/local modes are configured.
  • WindowsAzure.ServiceBus is declared, but no active application use was identified in the inspected source.

CatalogCatalogItemHiLoGenerator (Models/CatalogItemHiLoGenerator.cs)GetNextSequenceValueRetrieves the next identifier from a SQL sequence

There is no dedicated repository interface; CatalogService uses CatalogDBContext directly.

Caching Strategy

No catalog entity or query-result cache was identified. The application configures Redis-backed ASP.NET session state when enabled; this stores session state rather than catalog records. Mock mode uses the in-repository mock catalog service.

Data Ownership Boundaries

All catalog entities are owned by the Web Forms application and stored in the same SQL Server database. No cross-service database access, CQRS split, or distributed data composition was found. Catalog item rows reference brand and type rows through foreign keys. Image content is stored separately in Azure Blob Storage when that option is enabled; otherwise the mock image service references files beneath the application’s Pics directory.
